summary: The note describes the Greenhaven Wetlands Initiative (GWI), a community-led effort launched in September 2023 to restore Hazelton Marsh and other local wetlands. It covers the historical loss of wetlands, the use of drones, public education, scientific guidance, funding and invasive-species challenges, and plans to make the marsh a global research hub.
one_line: Greenhaven's Wetlands Initiative restores Hazelton Marsh through drones, education, science and partnerships, aiming to become a worldwide wetland research hub.
key_facts: The city of Greenhaven celebrated the commencement of Hazelton Marsh's restoration on September 5, 2023.
National Wetlands Inventory data suggests over 50% of America's wetlands have been lost since the 18th century, due to urbanization and agricultural expansion.
Mayor Thomas Eastwood led the launch of the Greenhaven Wetlands Initiative (GWI) on September 22, 2023.
The GWI partners with the Wetland Conservation Society and receives grants from the National Environmental Trust.
Drones are used for topographical surveys, seed dispersal, and wildlife population monitoring while minimizing human intrusion into sensitive habitats.
John Cartwright, chief environmental engineer on the project, said on October 15, 2023 that drones 'have revolutionized the way we approach conservation' and sped up restoration.
The GWI runs public workshops, school programs, and volunteer campaigns; teacher and volunteer coordinator Sarah Gomez spoke at a volunteer drive on October 29, 2023.
Ecologist Dr. Kevin Lin's research guided the selection of native plant species and water management meant to simulate natural hydrological cycles.
On September 30, 2023, Dr. Lin said 'Each wetland is unique' and restoration requires understanding each individual ecosystem.
Dr. Susan Watkins said in a November 10, 2023 interview that ignoring wetlands' distress signals 'is akin to undermining our own survival.'
Challenges for the GWI include funding, land acquisition, and combating invasive species; technology partnerships and local and national policy support helped overcome them.
Rachel Nguyen, the GWI's economic advisor, said the return on investment in ecosystem services and community well-being is immeasurable.
The GWI plans to establish Hazelton Marsh as a research hub for wetland conservationists worldwide.
